newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 takes another beating as jitters set in.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 takes another beating as jitters set in.

text.p: Czech shares took another pounding on Tuesday with major issues again taking most of the punishment.
The PX50 index fell 1.2 percent to close at 550.0 while the major issue dominated RPIX index lost nearly 1.5 percent to 1,112.
The worst hit company was power utility CEZ which has long been treated by dealers as the poor relation among the PX50's most heavily capitalised issues.
CEZ fell 24 crowns, 2.3 percent, to 1,023 -- its lowest level since May this year.

Analysts said CEZ's poor performance was attributable to concerns about the comany itself, especially over the deregulation of energy prices, and a general feeling of uncertainty about the Czech political and economic environment.
"There is all this speculation about energy prices and just general jitters," said Boris Gomez an analyst at ING Barings in Prague.
"The economic data coming out is being interpreted as negative and (premier) Klaus is neck and neck with (opposition leader) Zeman in the polls. Everywhere you look its negative," he said.

Last week, gross domestic product (GDP) figures showed growth in the second quarter of four percent - slower than in the first quarter and much lower than some of the Czech Republic's reformist neighbours.

Inflation, though low for the region at 9.6 percent, appears to have stabilised with few signs of a substantial downtrend in the near future, and there are concerns at the country's widening trade deficit.
Additionally, monetarist Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has lost ground in the opinion polls since the elections, when his centre-right coalition fell just short of a parliamentary majority.

Against such a background, the crisis at the country's largest fully private bank, Agrobanka, last week injected a distinct note of uncertainty into the equity market with foreigners particularly affected.
All major issues have lost ground and turnover has slumped in the last couple of days to less than 700 million crowns a session. REUTERS
